title: Wolfsklamm Gorge Stans
name: Wolfsklamm Gorge Stans
kurzbeschreibung: The Wolfsklamm near Stans: a deeply carved alpine gorge with 354 wooden steps, roaring waterfalls, and a historic pilgrimage trail to St. Georgenberg.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Wolfsklamm is located in the municipality of Stans in the Tyrolean Inntal in the Schwaz district at an altitude of around 560 to 898 metres. Nestled on the southern foothills of the Naturpark Karwendel, the gorge, opened to hikers in 1901, is considered one of the most beautiful and spectacular gorges in the European Alps. Rushing thunderously through limestone rock, the Stanser Bach has carved out an impressive natural monument over thousands of years that delights tens of thousands of nature lovers and hikers every year.

Natural Wonder & Pilgrimage Trail

The secured gorge trail leads along 354 artfully constructed wooden steps, wooden walkways, and galleries carved into vertical rock faces directly alongside the raging whitewater. Visitors experience emerald-green rock pools, foaming cascades, and imposing waterfalls up close, whose spray provides refreshing relief on hot summer days. The gorge walls rise sheer for over 100 metres in places. At the upper exit of the gorge, the valley widens into the broad riverbed of the Stanser Bach. From there, the historic pilgrimage trail crosses the Hohe Brücke – a monumental stone arch bridge dating from 1497 that is considered the oldest stone bridge in Tyrol – up to the oldest pilgrimage site in Tyrol, the rock-perched monastery of St. Georgenberg.

Visit & Getting There

Subject to weather conditions, the Wolfsklamm is open daily from 09:00 to 16:30 during the snow-free season from early May to late October (closed for safety reasons in heavy rain or snowfall; winter closure applies in winter). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, children and teenagers (6 to 14 years) approx. €2.00, toddlers free; holders of the regional Silbercard receive a discount. The proceeds support the ongoing maintenance of the elaborate wooden walkways. Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Schwaz or Jenbach), continue on the B171 to Stans, then follow signs to the gorge car park (parking fee applies). By public transport: train (ÖBB/S-Bahn) to the Stans bei Schwaz stop, from where a signposted, approx. 15-minute walk leads through the village directly to the gorge entrance.

Tips

Exploring the Wolfsklamm requires sturdy hiking boots with good grip and sure-footedness; the trail consists entirely of steps and is not suitable for wheelchairs or prams. Dogs on a leash are permitted. For the return journey, after stopping at the pilgrimage inn Gasthof St. Georgenberg, the gentler descent via the Maria-Tax-Weg back to Stans is recommended.
